sections.heading: AN ANIME OF USOTSUKI MII-KUN?
sections.content:
Q: I want to see an anime of Usotsuki Mii-kun to Kowareta Maa-chan. Isn't it getting an anime?

A: Even I have... things I don't know...[ref:mmr-quote] Honestly, isn't that book pretty difficult to adapt into anime? You could call it a downside of relying on narrative-trick storytelling.

sections.heading: WHY BECOME A NOVELIST AT ALL?
sections.content:
Q: In an earlier answer, you said you hated novels as a kid — so why did you decide to become a novelist? Have you ever thought about doing something else for a living?

A: I've never really thought about doing anything else, since my whole manner and personality are just kind of like that. As for why I became a novelist, there's no real reason. For whatever reason, it just felt like something I could do.

sections.heading: KARAOKE AND KARAOKE-SCREEN LYRICS
sections.content:
Q: By the way, have you been to karaoke recently? It might depend on the place, but it's a fun spot even just to sing your heart out alone. Also, about a bit of writing in Adachi to Shimamura — I sort of noticed this back around volume 7 of Denpa Onna[ref:denpa-onna-v7] too, but as long as there are lyrics scrolling along with the song, you can sing along even without remembering the words. So of course, the sense of clumsiness that comes through when Adachi and Shimamura, who haven't been to karaoke much, have to go look the lyrics up is also really cute.[ref:karaoke-lyrics-note]

A: I— I have been, actually... though that was maybe six years ago. I think I slept through about half of it. Thanks for pointing that out.

sections.heading: AN ENDING THAT DRIFTED OFF COURSE
sections.content:
Q: I'm writing a novel, and even though I really should have worked out the ending first, I just can't manage it — the ending ended up drifting about 45 degrees off from what I'd originally planned. By the way, I'd also like to be your rival.

A: I'm not about to hand salt to a rival![ref:salt-idiom] Why not just write the ending first? You can use that ending as an anchor to keep the story you originally had in mind on track.

sections.heading: AN UNFORTUNATE SIDE EFFECT
sections.content:
Q: Every time I read one of your books, I get so excited my heart starts racing. As a result, I suddenly end up with an intense urge to go to the bathroom, both ways. What should I do about this?

A: Go read it in the bathroom, then. Just like the professor from Naughty Trio.[ref:naughty-trio]

sections.heading: A READER'S PLOT SUBMISSION
sections.content:
Q: Here's a novel idea from an ordinary person. I came up with a story where the protagonist gathers together a group of runaway children to take revenge on each of their own parents, but it was such a hassle to actually write that I'm just handing the idea over to you instead. The ending is that the revenge fails completely, and every child except the protagonist ends up killed by their own parent. Just like in volume six of Usotsuki Mii-kun, the abnormal situation drives the plan into madness, and everyone just wants to die! I'd love to read a story about the protagonist slowly being backed into a psychological corner.

A: If you've already got the ending figured out, then just write it yourself! Turning your own imagination into something concrete is tedious and embarrassing, sure, but it's also a lot of fun.

sections.heading: PLANS BEYOND FIVE YEARS
sections.content:
Q: You've already had your five-year anniversary — do you still feel like keeping this up for another five, or even ten more years after that?

A: If there's demand for it, I'd like to keep going. So please, keep supporting me!

sections.heading: A MARRIAGE PROPOSAL
sections.content:
Q: Sensei!! I love you so much!! I really do!! Once I turn sixteen, can we get married??[ref:marriage-age]

A: Please don't...

sections.heading: MAKING THE CONTENT RICHER
sections.content:
Q: Even when I manage to write out a full setup-development-twist-conclusion structure, the content itself never feels substantial enough. Please tell me the trick!!!

A: The trick, huh... what would that even be? I'd love to know myself. It seems like all you can really do is write the story and then add more chapters afterward. Also — as for a sequel to Usotsuki Mii-kun... if it ever gets an anime adaptation, I could write ten, even twenty more volumes, ha ha ha.

sections.heading: THREE FAVORITE ANIME
sections.content:
Q: Please tell me three anime you like. Also, what do you like about each of them?

A: Probably these three, since I have a soft spot for mecha anime — and the one currently airing, Suisei no Gargantia, has been a lot of fun too.[ref:mecha-anime-list]

sections.heading: N743327's UPDATE SCHEDULE
sections.content:
Q: I know you're probably busy, but when will the web novel N743327 get its next update? Also, is there any chance it'll eventually be published as a proper light novel? If it's possible, please consider it.

A: Hmm... since it was already made available for free once, I kind of don't feel great about turning it into a paid book... those chapters weren't written to double as some kind of preview or trial material. As for the update... please, just a bit more patience. Sorry.[ref:n743327-fate]

sections.heading: THE MOVE TO "KAMAKURA PREFECTURE"
sections.content:
Q: When on earth are you actually moving to Kamakura Prefecture already?! I'm tired of waiting! (angry)[ref:kamakura-prefecture]

A: Even after saying I'd take a taxi to Kamakura Prefecture, I still never actually got taken there...[ref:kamakura-subject]

sections.heading: TOO MANY SERIES AT ONCE?
sections.content:
Q: Aren't you running too many series at the same time over at Dengeki Bunko? I'm curious about the continuation of every single one of them, so please split yourself into pieces and write them all, pretty please.[ref:concurrent-series]

A: With the Four-Witches Fist,[ref:four-witches-fist] I wonder if the stuff inside your head gets split into four parts too.

sections.heading: A HANASAKI TAROU SEQUEL, AGAIN
sections.content:
Q: Nice to meet you. I'm a fan of both Usotsuki Mii-kun and Hanasaki Tarou. Is a sequel to the Hanasaki Tarou series planned for publication? I especially love the husband-and-wife comedy routine between Momohime and Hanasaki Tarou!

A: Calling them husband and wife — isn't that technically a crime?[ref:momohime-age] ...As for a sequel, well, if it sells just a bit better...

sections.heading: ADACHI TO SHIMAMURA'S FUTURE
sections.content:
Q: Adachi to Shimamura is so much fun! Is there going to be a sequel?!

A: Thank you. There probably will be.

sections.heading: SIX DAYS, SIX PEOPLE, SIX GUNS — STILL WAITING
sections.content:
Q: I love you so, so much, Iruma-sensei. Really, really, so much, I love you to bits. By the way, is there still no continuation of Six Days, Six People, Six Guns? I feel like I'm being kept waiting on purpose, sensei, you ///

A: Well, as for the continuation... um, since it hasn't been selling that well... I'll do my best.[ref:six-days-guns-timeline]

sections.heading: TAKING ON A MIDDLE SCHOOLER AS A DISCIPLE
sections.content:
Q: I'm only in my second year of middle school, but how can I become your disciple? I mean this sincerely. You're such a humble teacher, and I want to be your student. ((serious face))

A: Since I don't know how to actually teach anyone, I don't take on disciples. Sorry.

sections.heading: WHY BECOME A NOVELIST?
sections.content:
Q: Why did you want to become a novelist in the first place?

A: Because I was bored. By the way, I'm the same age as the self-proclaimed god of the new world.[ref:light-yagami]

sections.heading: IS THE JOB FUN?
sections.content:
Q: Do you enjoy the work?

A: If it were fun all the time, it wouldn't really be work! ...Jokes aside, since I'm always repeating the same process over and over, I do get a little tired of it sometimes, though I wouldn't say I find it boring.

sections.heading: A TYPO CORRECTION
sections.content:
Q: I'm sure plenty of people have already pointed this out, but on page 141, line 5 of Yuiitsu no Negai, shouldn't that name be "Mizukawa" rather than "Mizuguchi"?

A: Thank you for the report. If there's ever a reprint, we'll get that fixed. ...I— if there ever is one.

sections.heading: RECOMMENDED READING FROM YOUR INFLUENCES
sections.content:
Q: I read somewhere on a wiki that when asked which authors influenced you, you named Nisio Isin, Otsuichi, and Honobu Yonezawa. Could you recommend a work from each of those three authors?

A: Hmm... I really haven't been reading anything lately, so I can't really make recommendations. I did name them at some point, but that feels like it was years ago now.

sections.heading: HOW TO BECOME YOUR GIRLFRIEND
sections.content:
Q: What would it take to become your girlfriend?

A: I don't think there's any particular requirement... nobody's asking you to go fetch the jewel from Mount Hōrai or anything.[ref:hourai-jewel] That said, you're probably better off giving up on that one...

sections.heading: JOINING THE IRUMA ARMY
sections.content:
Q: I'd like to join the Iruma Army too. Once I become a novelist myself, please let me enlist.

A: All right, recruit number two![ref:iruma-army]

sections.heading: MORE TAMAKO AND KIIRODORI
sections.content:
Q: I'd love to see that pair of weirdos from Tamako to Kiiro-dori again.

A: If I can come up with something, I'll write a short story about them.

sections.heading: A PRINT EDITION OF ADACHI TO SHIMAMURA
sections.content:
Q: Will the book version of Adachi to Shimamura keep coming out?

A: The plan is to publish it once the serialized portion has built up enough material. P— probably, yes.

sections.heading: N743327 AND LZEEHLN UPDATES
sections.content:
Q: Have N743327 and LZEEHLN still not gotten any new updates?

A: P— please, just a bit more patience.[ref:lzeehln-fate]

sections.heading: CAN A NOVELIST MAKE MONEY?
sections.content:
Q: Can novelists actually make money?

A: The general public seems to think you can't, but as long as your work sells well, you can. That's probably true of just about any profession.

sections.heading: MORE HANASAKI TAROU AND KISOGAWA
sections.content:
Q: I really love the Hanasaki Tarou series, and I love Kisogawa too. Is a sequel planned for publication?

A: Something with absolutely zero mystery elements is probably something I could actually write.

sections.heading: A COIL SCHOOL-DAYS SPINOFF?
sections.content:
Q: I'd love to read a story told from the point of view of Dr. Koi Renji, about her and the other doctors' school days.

A: I hadn't thought about that at all... if some kind of inspiration strikes, I'll try writing it.

sections.heading: A LIGHTHEARTED QUESTION
sections.content:
Q: Hello, I've always loved your work and the "Iruma no Ma" site. Your books are so charming that after reading them, I get the feeling you must be really popular in person too. Just as a side question — could someone whose chest size is only a sixth of Yuzu-yuzu's still become your girlfriend?[ref:yuzu-yuzu]

A: A charming body of work doesn't necessarily equal me being popular in person... N— no, that's not really equivalent... Also, um, well, there's that saying that the bigger option covers the smaller one too...[ref:big-covers-small]

sections.heading: ONE MORE RECRUIT
sections.content:
Q: I'm also aiming to become a novelist — if it's possible, could you let me join the Iruma Army?

A: All right, recruit number three! What a bumper crop this is!

references.title: MMR: Magazine Mystery Report
references.note: "Even I have things I don't know" is a signature catchphrase of Kibayashi, the leader character in the manga MMR: Magazine Mystery Report, serialized in Weekly Shonen Magazine. Kibayashi and the other members of the fictional "MMR" investigative team were modeled directly on real Weekly Shonen Magazine editors of the time. Kibayashi in particular was based on editor Shin Kibayashi, who later left editing to become a manga writer under a number of pen names, most notably Seimaru Amagi, credited on The Kindaichi Case Files, as well as Psychometrer Eiji and GetBackers.

references.title: Denpa Onna to Seishun Otoko, Volume 7
references.note: The questioner references having first noticed this quirk of karaoke lyric displays while reading the seventh volume of Iruma's earlier series Denpa Onna to Seishun Otoko.

references.title: A Continuity Note on Karaoke Scenes
references.note: In the "Joshikousei Holiday" chapter of the first volume of Adachi to Shimamura, the karaoke scene repeatedly references the characters trying to 'remember the lyrics' or 'not knowing the lyrics.' In reality, karaoke machine screens generally display the lyrics on-screen as the song plays, which makes memorization largely unnecessary. This appears to be an oversight on Iruma's part, one the questioner is gently pointing out here.

references.title: "Sending Salt to an Enemy"
references.note: A well-known Japanese idiom (teki ni shio wo okuru) meaning to help out a rival or opponent, traditionally traced back to a legend about the warlord Uesugi Kenshin supplying salt to his enemy Takeda Shingen. Iruma jokingly declines to do this for a self-declared rival.

references.title: Naughty Trio (Chappagakkou no Sannin-gumi / literally "Bad Kids Trio")
references.source: Children's Book Series by Masamoto Nasu
references.note: A long-running Japanese children's book series by author Masamoto Nasu, referenced here for a scene in which one of its characters reads while in the bathroom.

references.title: Legal Marriage Age in Japan (pre-2022)
references.note: Prior to a 2022 revision of Japanese civil law, the minimum legal marriage age was 16 for women and 18 for men, which is the basis of the questioner's math here.

references.title: Iruma's Favorite Mecha Anime
references.note: Iruma names three earlier mecha anime alongside Suisei no Gargantia (Gargantia on the Verdurous Planet), which was airing at the time of this Q&A in the spring 2013 season. A translator's note in the original source adds that the chapter titles of volume 4 of Adachi to Shimamura are drawn from episode titles of one of these three earlier series; we were unable to conclusively verify the specific English titles of all three works from the Chinese source and have left the identification of that trio open.

references.title: N743327's Eventual Fate
references.note: N743327 was one of Iruma's serialized works published on his official website between October 2, 2011 and May 24, 2013, reaching five chapters total. Despite Iruma's assurance here that an update was coming, the story was never continued after this point.

references.title: "Kamakura Prefecture"
references.note: Kamakura is technically a city within Kanagawa Prefecture, not a prefecture itself — 'Kamakura Prefecture' is a running joke Iruma uses repeatedly, including in the afterword of Tokage no Ou II, where he refers to his father as someone who 'thinks of himself as a citizen of Kamakura Prefecture (that's not a typo).' Iruma mentioned moving to Kamakura multiple times starting around 2012, but the move didn't actually happen until 2017. After the move, the setting of several of Iruma's works shifted away from his native Gifu and Nagoya toward Kamakura, as in Mou Hitotsu no Inochi, Mou Hitori no Majo, and Kanchuu no Kanaria. Iruma's father also appears to have a strong personal connection to Kamakura, and several stories he has serialized on Iruma's official site are likewise set there.

references.title: An Ambiguous Subject
references.note: The original Japanese answer omits its subject, so it's unclear exactly who is meant to have taken the taxi and who failed to be taken to Kamakura — it could be Iruma himself, his father, or even the questioner. One plausible reading is: 'Even when I told my father to take a taxi to Kamakura, he never actually took me there.'

references.title: Iruma's Concurrent Series in April 2013
references.note: At the time of this Q&A, Iruma was simultaneously serializing Tokage no Ou and Six Days, Six People, Six Guns, with the first volume of a new series, Mugen Loop Game, confirmed for release the following month, and a sequel to Adachi to Shimamura already tentatively planned. Of these four ongoing projects, Six Days, Six People, Six Guns eventually ended on a truncated, cut-short note, Tokage no Ou and Mugen Loop Game were both discontinued without ever reaching a conclusion, and only Adachi to Shimamura has continued publication to the present day, if somewhat precariously at times.

references.title: Shishinken (Four-Body Fist)
references.note: A reference to Tenshinhan's signature technique from Dragon Ball, which splits his body into four copies. Iruma jokes that whatever's inside his own head must have gotten split up the same way, given how many series he's juggling at once.

references.title: Momohime's Age
references.note: Momohime, the character the questioner is referring to as Hanasaki Tarou's 'wife,' is only thirteen years old in the story, which is the basis of Iruma's joking objection here.

references.title: Light Yagami
references.note: The 'self-proclaimed god of the new world' is Light Yagami, protagonist of the manga and anime Death Note, whose canonical birth year of 1986 matches Iruma Hitoma's own.

references.title: The Jeweled Branch of Mount Hōrai
references.source: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter
references.note: One of five impossible bridal tasks that Princess Kaguya assigns to her suitors in the classical Japanese folktale The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter — in this case, retrieving a jeweled branch from the mythical Mount Hōrai. Iruma uses it here as a stand-in for an impossibly difficult condition, only to say that no such condition exists for dating him.

references.title: The Iruma Army's Second Recruit
references.note: One other fan had already been promised a spot in the 'Iruma Army' during the second round of this Q&A column, making this questioner the second confirmed recruit.

references.title: Six Days, Six People, Six Guns Publication Timeline
references.note: The first volume of Six Days, Six People, Six Guns was published in August 2012. Its second volume followed in December 2013, after this Q&A was posted, and its third and final volume — which brought the series to an abrupt, truncated ending — wasn't published until January 2016.

references.title: N743327 and LZEEHLN
references.note: Neither of these two web serials ultimately received any further updates after this point, despite Iruma's request here for a little more patience.

references.title: Yuzuyuzu Fushimi
references.source: Character from Usotsuki Mii-kun to Kowareta Maa-chan
references.note: Yuzuyuzu Fushimi is a large-chested character from Usotsuki Mii-kun to Kowareta Maa-chan, used here by the questioner as a jokey unit of measurement.

references.title: "The Bigger One Covers the Smaller"
references.note: A Japanese proverb (dai wa shou wo kaneru), roughly equivalent to 'the more can stand in for the less,' which Iruma invokes here as a lighthearted, noncommittal response to the question.
